name: Athi River
blurb: Last big town before the plains. Fuel, supermarkets and the start of the open road.
tip: Fill the tank here, the next big stop is a long way.

name: Lukenya Hill
blurb: A rocky hill popular with climbers and hikers, just off the highway after Athi River.
tip: A short scramble gives a wide view back towards Nairobi.

name: Machakos Town
blurb: One of Kenya's oldest towns, a short detour off the highway with hills all around.
tip: Try the roadside roast maize and the mango sellers in season.

name: Emali
blurb: The junction town where the road to Amboseli leaves the Mombasa highway.
tip: Good place for a snack and a stretch before the Amboseli turn.

name: Hunter's Lodge, Kiboko
blurb: A classic old stopover beside a spring-fed pool full of birds, halfway to the coast.
tip: Lunch under the trees, watch the weavers and kingfishers.

name: Makindu Sikh Temple
blurb: A gurdwara that has welcomed travellers of every faith for a century, with free meals and a quiet garden.
tip: Cover your head, remove shoes, and leave a donation if you eat.

name: Kibwezi Forest
blurb: A pocket of indigenous forest with springs, butterflies and birds, a green surprise in dry country.
tip: The forest is looked after with the Sheldrick Trust and the lodge inside is for foster parents, so check access before you turn off.

name: Mtito Andei
blurb: The halfway town between Nairobi and Mombasa, and the gate town for Tsavo.
tip: Last reliable fuel and food before the long Tsavo stretch.

name: Tsavo River Bridge
blurb: Where the highway crosses the Tsavo River, with the park on both sides and often elephants near the water.
tip: Slow down and look, but do not stop on the bridge itself.

name: Voi
blurb: The town between Tsavo East and the Taita Hills, with lodges and the park's main gate close by.
tip: Turn off here for Tsavo East or the Taita Hills.

name: Taita Hills
blurb: Cool forested hills rising above the dry Tsavo plains, with cloud forest and rare birds.
tip: A long detour, but a cool night's sleep after the heat.

name: Mackinnon Road Mosque
blurb: A small mosque beside the highway that marks the grave of a railway-era Muslim saint, a place of pilgrimage.
tip: Visitors are welcome, dress modestly and ask before photos.

name: Mariakani
blurb: The last town before Mombasa, where the coast heat and the coconut palms begin.
tip: Buy madafu, young coconut water, from the roadside.

name: Rift Valley Viewpoint
blurb: The escarpment edge where the floor of the Great Rift Valley suddenly opens below you, with Longonot in the distance.
tip: Stop at the curio stalls early, before the tour buses.

name: Mai Mahiu Catholic Church
blurb: A tiny chapel built by Italian prisoners of war in the 1940s while they built the escarpment road.
tip: A five minute stop, right beside the road at the bottom of the hill.

name: Mount Longonot
blurb: The volcano with a bite out of its top, a steep half day hike to the crater rim.
tip: Start early, there is no shade on the climb.

name: Hell's Gate
blurb: Cycle among zebra and giraffe between red cliffs, a short detour south of Naivasha.
tip: Hire bikes at the gate, go early.

name: Lake Naivasha
blurb: The freshwater lake with hippos, pelicans and fish eagles, two hours from Nairobi.
tip: A boat ride at sunrise is the best hour on the lake.

name: Lake Elmenteita Viewpoint
blurb: A highway lay-by looking down on the soda lake and the Sleeping Warrior hills.
tip: Pelicans and flamingos are often visible from the road.

name: Kariandusi Prehistoric Site
blurb: Stone tools lying where early humans left them, with a small museum, just off the highway.
tip: Combine it with the Elmenteita viewpoint next door.

name: Lake Nakuru National Park
blurb: The compact park around a soda lake, the easiest place to see rhino in Kenya.
tip: Main gate is minutes from Nakuru town.

name: Menengai Crater
blurb: A giant caldera on the edge of Nakuru, drive to the rim in minutes.
tip: Windy and wide, bring a jacket.

name: Ngong Hills
blurb: The ridge walk on the edge of the Rift, with Nairobi on one side and the valley on the other.
tip: Hire a ranger at the gate for the full ridge.

name: Kajiado
blurb: The Maasai county town, with a busy livestock market and beadwork on sale.
tip: Market days are the liveliest, ask locally which day.

name: Namanga
blurb: The border town with Tanzania, in the shadow of Namanga Hill, with Maasai craft markets by the road.
tip: Bargain gently and in good humour.

name: Kimana
blurb: The gateway town to Amboseli's eastern side, with a community wildlife sanctuary and the first clear views of Kilimanjaro.
tip: Fuel up here, there is none in the park.

name: Kilimanjaro Viewpoint, Kimana road
blurb: On the approach to Kimana the land opens up and Kilimanjaro fills the sky on a clear morning.
tip: Pull well off the road for photos, the mountain is clearest before 9am.

name: Chyulu Hills
blurb: Young green volcanic hills with lava tubes and huge views, a proper detour between Emali and Tsavo West.
tip: Rough roads, go in a 4x4.

name: Thika
blurb: The pineapple town, with the Chania and Thika falls right beside the old road.
tip: Stop at the falls behind the old Blue Posts hotel.

name: Fourteen Falls
blurb: A wide set of waterfalls on the Athi River near Thika, best after the rains.
tip: Go with a local guide, and keep away from the edge.

name: Ol Donyo Sabuk
blurb: A lone forested mountain east of Thika with buffalo, a summit road and views of both Mount Kenya and Kilimanjaro.
tip: A small KWS park, drive or hike to the top.

name: Mwea Rice Fields
blurb: Flat green paddies stretching to the horizon, Kenya's rice bowl, beside the road through Mwea.
tip: Buy a bag of pishori rice from the roadside stalls.

name: Sagana
blurb: The white water rafting stretch of the Tana River, with camps on the bank.
tip: Book a rafting trip ahead, mornings are calmer.

name: Nanyuki Equator Line
blurb: The sign where the road crosses the equator, with the water-draining demonstration everyone falls for.
tip: Stand with a foot in each hemisphere for the photo.

name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy
blurb: The conservancy with the last two northern white rhinos, minutes from Nanyuki.
tip: Book the rhino visit ahead.

name: Trout Tree, Nanyuki
blurb: A restaurant built up in a fig tree over trout ponds, a favourite lunch stop on the Mount Kenya road.
tip: Colobus monkeys in the branches, keep an eye on your bread.

name: Kinangop Plateau
blurb: High, cold farmland under the Aberdares on the old road to Nakuru, with wide skies and potato fields.
tip: Carry a jacket, it is cold up here.

name: Kericho Tea Fields
blurb: Rolling green tea as far as you can see, with pickers in the rows and afternoon rain most days.
tip: Stop at a tea estate gate for a tasting.

name: Kisumu Lakeside
blurb: Lake Victoria's waterfront, where the fish is fried fresh and the sunsets are long.
tip: Order tilapia and ugali at Dunga Beach.

name: Kit Mikayi
blurb: The balanced boulders sacred to the Luo, west of Kisumu.
tip: Take a local guide into the rocks.

name: Kakamega Forest
blurb: Kenya's only tropical rainforest, with monkeys, butterflies and dawn walks.
tip: Hire a community guide.

name: Nyali Bridge Viewpoint
blurb: The crossing from Mombasa island to the north coast, with the creek and the dhows below.
tip: Best at sunset from the north bank.

name: Mtwapa Creek
blurb: A tidal creek lined with seafood restaurants and boat moorings on the way north.
tip: Try the prawns at a creekside table.

name: Kilifi Creek
blurb: A deep blue creek crossed by a long bridge, with sailing boats and a laid-back town on the north bank.
tip: Stop on the Kilifi side for a swim at the creek beach.

name: Gedi Ruins
blurb: The Swahili stone town swallowed by forest, just off the Malindi road.
tip: Take a guide at the gate.

name: Mida Creek Boardwalk
blurb: A long boardwalk through mangroves to a sunset platform, run by the local community.
tip: Low tide for wading birds, sunset for the light.

name: Likoni Ferry
blurb: The famous ferry across Kilindini harbour, the only way south from Mombasa island by road.
tip: Walk on if you can, the car queues are long at rush hour.

name: Shimba Hills
blurb: Cool forest hills above the south coast, with sable antelope and Sheldrick Falls.
tip: A half day detour from Diani.

name: Shimoni
blurb: The end of the south coast road, with the slave caves and the boats to Wasini and the marine park.
tip: Boats leave early for the best snorkelling.
